newsitem.title: USA: McLeod Inc loss reflects expansion costs.
newsitem.headline: McLeod Inc loss reflects expansion costs.

text.p: McLeod Inc, a provider of integrated telecommunications services, on Friday said its losses for the fourth quarter and the full year widened primarily because of expansion costs.

It said the doubling of its net loss in 1996 to $22.3 million reflected an expansion of its local and long-distance business. The company also cited costs related to acquisitions completed in 1996 and amortization expense related to stock options granted certain officers, employees and directors.
At the end of 1996, McLeod had 65,367 local lines and 17,794 telecommunications customers, compared with 35,795 local lines and 8,776 telecommunications customers the previous year.
While McLeod's loss widened in the fourth quarter, its revenue increased by $26.3 million to $35.8 million.

Local and long distance telecommunications service revenues rose $5.6 million, revenue related to network activities increased $1 million. Ruffalo, Cody & Associates Inc, acquired in July, and McLeodUSA Publishing Group, a business acquired in September, contributed a total of $19.7 million.
For the quarter, McLeod posted a loss of $8.9 million, or $0.18 a share, compared with a loss of $3.2 million, or $0.09, in the year-earlier quarter. Revenues rose to $35.8 million from $9.6 million.
For the year, the company lost $22.3 million, or $0.52 a share, compared with a 1995 loss $11.3 million, or $0.31. Revenues advanced to $81.3 million from $29 million.
The 1996 full-year revenue would have been $57.6 million without the acquisitions of Ruffalo, Cody and McLeodUSA Publishing Group, formerly known as Telecom*USA Publishing Group Inc.
